fact: RFI reports that Angola's National Assembly adopted a cybersecurity law on 12 August 2026 by 104 votes (MPLA) to 56 (UNITA); the report does not say it was promulgated or in force.

PTI reports that the National Assembly approved the Cybersecurity Bill (Proposta de Lei da Cibersegurança) in global vote on 12 August 2026, 104 for, 54 against, no abstentions; the report does not say it was promulgated or in force.

ANGOP reports that the National Assembly adopted the cybersecurity law on 12 August 2026, 104 votes (MPLA) to 56 (UNITA), with fines of 7 to 4,000 national minimum wages by gravity; it does not say the law was promulgated or in force.
Novo Jornal reports that the National Assembly approved the Cybersecurity Bill in general terms on 23 January 2026, 105 for, 1 against and 75 UNITA abstentions.

A UNITA deputy, quoted by Novo Jornal, says Law 7/17 of 16 February (protection of computer networks and systems) is part of the current legal order and the bill would repeal it; the report dates nothing about Law 7/17 beyond its 2017 enactment, so as_of is the report's publication date.

fact: INACOM reports that on 27 October 2025 the Council of Ministers considered the Cybersecurity Bill (Proposta de Lei da Cibersegurança) for sending to the National Assembly.

Angola's delegation to the IDEA 2026 forum in Lusaka (27-29 July 2026) said its cybersecurity law was still at the diagnosis stage, as reported by Angop; the date is the report's published date, 2026-07-29, since the statement is made at the forum's close.

Telecompaper reports the National Assembly's specialised committees approved the proposed Cybersecurity Law, which was not yet in force; the document gives no event date, so its published date 2026-08-10 is used.
Angola's minister said the Cybersecurity Law has entered into force.
Angola's Council of Ministers on 27 October 2025 cleared the Cybersecurity Bill, presented by MINTTICS in February 2025, for final treatment in Parliament.
